system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Two-round self-training: regenerating pseudo-masks from MVFA's own adapted features
SUMMARY: Train MVFA on label-restricted pseudo-masks from frozen CLIP features, then regenerate the pseudo-masks with the trained model's adapted segmentation features and retrain once.
HYPOTHESIS: A second round of pseudo-mask generation from MVFA's own adapted level-4 segmentation features raises pseudo-mask Dice against true masks by at least 8 points over round-1 pseudo-masks from frozen CLIP features, and the round-2 model recovers at least 5 points more of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: Superpixel snapping and DINOv2 propagation both import a better notion of image structure from outside MVFA, either raw intensity or a second backbone. The common explanation of their gain is that frozen CLIP features are a poor basis for localisation. MVFA's adapters are trained precisely to recalibrate CLIP features toward anomaly localisation (the paper's central claim), so after one round of training on noisy pseudo-masks the adapted features should separate lesion from normal tissue better than frozen CLIP features, and pseudo-masks regenerated from them should be cleaner. This self-training route uses the target method's own mechanism instead of an external prior, and image-level labels keep it anchored: regeneration is restricted to images labelled abnormal, which prevents the confirmation drift that unlabelled self-training suffers.
METHOD: 1) Round 1: make_pseudo_masks.py with frozen CLIP layer-24 features (label-restricted rule, 99th percentile on source validation); train MVFA with train_zero.py as usual. 2) Round 2: extract the trained model's adapted seg features at level 4 (output of seg_adapters[3] mixed residually) for normal and abnormal source training images; recompute normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation, threshold at the 99th percentile, and regenerate masks for abnormal images only. 3) Retrain from the CLIP initialisation (not from round 1) on the round-2 masks to avoid accumulating overfitting. 4) Stop after two rounds; a third round is an ablation. Hyper-parameters as MVFA; selection on source validation against the current round's pseudo-masks.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; round 1; round 2; round 3 (ablation); masks removed from all 3 masked sources and the image-only datasets added as pseudo-mask sources. Ablation: round 2 without label restriction (regenerate on all images). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per round, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if round-2 pseudo-mask Dice does not exceed round 1 by 8 points or the round-2 model does not improve pixel AUROC by 5 points of recovered gain.

Idea B:
TITLE: SAM2-formed pseudo-masks from label-restricted patch prompts for mask-free MVFA localisation
SUMMARY: Prompt SAM2 with the most anomalous label-restricted patches of each abnormal source image and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the returned masks.
HYPOTHESIS: SAM2-formed pseudo-masks with 3 positive prompts raise pseudo-mask Dice by at least 12 points over patch pseudo-masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type: true masks; patch pseudo-masks (problem rule); SAM2-formed pseudo-masks with n_points in {1, 3, 5} positive prompts (patch centres with the largest NN distance above threshold, at least 2 patches apart) and 3 negative prompts from the lowest-distance patches. Masks whose area exceeds 40% of the image or whose overlap with the patch pseudo-mask is below 0.2 are rejected (fallback to the patch pseudo-mask). Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice vs true masks; trained model's pixel AUROC and Dice on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: Label-restricted pseudo-masks give reliable locations but poor shapes. PSMP-CLIP shows that point prompts sampled from patch anomaly evidence let SAM2 produce precise masks, and AA-CLIP shows that separated anchors make the patch evidence cleaner. Using SAM2 as a mask former on top of the problem's pseudo-mask seeds should produce lesion-shaped targets for MVFA's segmentation adapters without any human masks.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute patch NN distances and the label-restricted rule. 2) sam_refine.py: load SAM2 (hiera-base-plus checkpoint from the official repository); for each abnormal source image, select up to n_points positive patch centres (scaled to image coordinates) and 3 negative ones; call SAM2ImagePredictor.predict(point_coords, point_labels, multimask_output=True) and keep the mask with the highest predicted IoU. 3) Apply the rejection rules; save masks. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py loads them; train_zero.py unchanged (Focal + Dice). 5) n_points selected on source validation (where source masks exist). Runtime: one SAM2 call per abnormal image. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; patch pseudo-masks; SAM2-formed with 1/3/5 points; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: without rejection rules; MedSAM-style medical SAM weights if available as an alternative mask former. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice/IoU and rejection rate; trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if SAM2 masks do not improve pseudo-mask Dice by at least 5 points on at least two of the three masked datasets.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>

CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
